answer_text:
Let

\[
I_n=\int_0^\infty \frac{n^2 \sin(x/n)}{n^3x+x(1+x^3)}\,dx
=\int_0^\infty \frac{n^2 \sin(x/n)}{x(n^3+x^3+1)}\,dx.
\]

Make the scaling substitution

\[
x=nt,\qquad dx=n\,dt.
\]

Then

\[
I_n=\int_0^\infty
\frac{n^2\sin t}{nt\left(n^3+n^3t^3+1\right)}\,n\,dt.
\]

Simplifying,

\[
I_n
= \frac{1}{n}\int_0^\infty
\frac{\sin t}{t(1+t^3)}
\cdot
\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{n^3(1+t^3)}}\,dt.
\]

The extra factor satisfies

\[
0\le
\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{n^3(1+t^3)}}\le 1.
\]

Also, the function

\[
\frac{\sin t}{t(1+t^3)}
\]

is integrable on \((0,\infty)\): near \(0\), \(\sin t/t\to 1\), and for large \(t\),

\[
\left|\frac{\sin t}{t(1+t^3)}\right|\le \frac{1}{t^4}.
\]

Hence there exists a finite constant \(C\) such that

\[
|I_n|
\le \frac{1}{n}\int_0^\infty
\left|\frac{\sin t}{t(1+t^3)}\right|dt
\le \frac{C}{n}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} I_n=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]

27B·v4.method: Substitution x = nt reduces the integral to (1/n) times a convergent integral, giving limit 0.
